requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.sources.css.fingerprints`. All three obligations are exercised and asserted.

**Comments excluded from CSS structural hashes**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a CSS case that selects `rule[a]` in `a.css`. It shows that changing the comment text (`/* note */` to `/* other note */`) leaves the hash unchanged. It shows that removing the comment leaves the hash unchanged. It also shows that changing a non-comment word (`red` to `blue`) changes the hash, so the equality assertions are not trivial.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` repeats this for CSS. Its `/* note */` and `/* edited */` variants hash equal.
- The CSS profile (`static[PROFILE]` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/css.rs`) sets `hashes_comment: never`. This matches the expectation that CSS hashes no comments. I used it only to confirm that comments are excluded for every CSS comment, not to judge the implementation.

**Whitespace-separated words, hashed per word (`requirements.references.structural_hash`, cited)**
- The CSS case in the same test uses `content: "two words"` for the original and `content: "two   words"` for the variant. The two fingerprints must be equal, so whitespace is not hashed. It uses `content: "twowords"` as the third variant, which must differ, so each word is encoded separately and `ab cd` differs from `abcd`.

**SHA-256 digest**
- The same loop asserts that each fingerprint value is 64 characters long and all ASCII hex digits, which is the shape of a SHA-256 digest. It doesn't check a known-answer vector, but that general property belongs to `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which is cited here and not reassessed.

**Fingerprint scheme (`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, cited)**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` checks `languages::Css.fingerprint_scheme()` against `"css-structural-v1"`. It also checks that `OutlineContent::from_source(...).fingerprint_scheme()` retains that scheme. The retention check uses the inferred path, and the equivalent assertion for the explicit-language path is not made. That check compares the explicit and inferred fingerprints instead.
- The rule that changing the calculation requires a new scheme can't be tested mechanically. It is also the cited requirement's own obligation.

All CSS-specific obligations have a test that both exercises the behavior and asserts the outcome. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
